critique.reason:
The proposed $3,000 credit is not supported by the contract. Section 4.2 credits only full hours of unavailability beyond the 99.9% monthly commitment in 4.1, and caps the credit at $1,000 per calendar month. The proposal applied 0.5% per hour to all six hours with no cap.

Calculation: September has 30 days, or 720 hours. At 99.9% availability, 0.72 hours of downtime is allowed. The incident lasted 6h15m (TCK-881), so about 5.53 hours exceed the commitment, which is 5 full hours. Five hours at 0.5% of $100,000 is $2,500. Section 4.2 caps this at $1,000, so the supported credit is $1,000. The cap binds even if the 99.9% allowance is ignored, since six full hours would give $3,000, which is also capped at $1,000. The $1,000 result holds under either reading.

The customer's claim in CRM-2207 is timely, since it was sent on 2026-09-26, within 30 days of the 2026-09-14 incident. The request is therefore valid, but the amount is not. Under 7.4, the customer may set off only a 4.2 credit. The customer deducted $3,000 and paid $97,000, so the $2,000 above the $1,000 credit is an unauthorized set-off. After a $1,000 credit memo, $2,000 of INV-1001 remains open and should be collected. The payment itself was received on time under Net 30 (due 2026-10-01).
